- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.67) — model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices after sentiment dips (especially <0.33) — model underreacts to bearish sentiment, leading to lagged corrections.
- Model consistently overpredicts near-term (1-3 day) price movements after spikes, then corrects — apply mean reversion bias for 3-5 day horizons.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust downward by 1–2% for 5–7 day forecasts.
- For long-term (10+ day) forecasts, model tends to overfit recent trends — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is flat or negative.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment-driven momentum beyond 7 days — sentiment decay reduces forecast accuracy after 7-day horizon.
